notes.title: Endzone 2 Version 1.0 is out now!
notes.notes:
[p]Survivors,

The [b]full release of Endzone 2[/b] is here – and with it comes a whole new challenge: [b]Raiders[/b] have entered the wasteland! For the first time, enemy convoys threaten your settlements with [b]coordinated zone attacks[/b], [b]devastating artillery strikes[/b], and [b]daring resource raids[/b]. Every encounter is a [b]high‑stakes battle[/b] – [b]defend your people[/b] to claim victory, or [b]watch raiders escape[/b] with your hard‑earned supplies.

Will you rise to defend your settlement – or fall to the raider menace?[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="ztpog872bMA;full"][/previewyoutube][p]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]We have a little gift for you[/h2][p]
As a heartfelt thank you for your incredible support during Early Access and beyond, we're giving away a special piece of the journey: the [b]Endzone 2: Campfire Sessions [/b]Soundtrack. This special soundtrack features [b]five atmospheric songs[/b] that have, until now, only been heard in our trailers.[/p][p]The soundtrack is [b]free[/b] for everyone who owns Endzone 2—whether you've been with us from the start or just joined at release. It should appear automatically in your library ([b]for some it's already there, for others it might take a day or two[/b]).[/p][p]The offer is available until [b]two weeks after release[/b], so make sure to claim your copy in time.

[b]From all of us: thank you.[/b] ❤️[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/bb344e3298af174544f8d5721ba8775251d2762b.png"][/img][/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png"][/img][/p][h2]
Update Highlights Breakdown[/h2][p] [/p][h3][b]Raiders are back[/b][/h3][p]→ Raiders now roam and terrorize the wastelands [/p][h3][b]Combat mechanics[/b][/h3][p]→ To secure your settlement, vehicles can be equipped with weapons[/p][h3][b]New buildings[/b][/h3][p]→ Bunker, Monument to Defense, Decontamination lab  [/p][h3][b]New items[/b][/h3][p]→ New items have been added to stand a chance against raiders[/p][h3][b]New and updated expeditions[/b][/h3][p]→ Expedition that has new items to loot, and to further enhance infrastructures  [/p][h3][b]Audio Update[/b][/h3][p]→ New voiceovers, rabble sounds, attack barks and feedback lines[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/0f7082681f7f7023d00dbc307f6ea16547e11bde.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2366561470be835a56cc4e8df467f98779495d78.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Audio:[/b] Added new voiceovers, rabble sounds, and attack barks.
[b]Audio:[/b] Added new VO feedback for vehicle destruction and spawning.
[b]Audio:[/b] Implemented settler click barks for zone attacks.
[b]Buildings:[/b] Added a bunker building that can be placed in the badlands using the Pioneer in order to defend territory against raiders. In order for bunkers to work they need to be equipped with a weapon item.
[b]Buildings:[/b] Buildings in the badlands can now be repaired with Iron Tools using the Pioneer.
[b]Buildings:[/b] Added a new monument that can be unlocked through a side mission that focusses on defeating raiders.
[b]Buildings:[/b] Added Decontamination lab that produces decontamination kits.[/p][p][/p][table noborder="1" equalcells="1" colwidth=",,229"][tr][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/36d16af0f25962c2f02ca89a73296290b264720b.png"][/img][/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/15bd92cc15cdc04691829691821298ceb958edaf.png"][/img][/p][/td][td colwidth="229"][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a6e79e9a4ac86a26316c1445785e0d3c6b3469a2.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][b]Expeditions:[/b] Added new expeditions where weapon items can be found.
[b]Expeditions:[/b] Added a new expedition that provides electricity when completed.
[b]Expeditions:[/b] Resource mines in the badlands now profit from electricity networks.
[b]Items:[/b] Added various weapon items that can be found on expeditions or purchased at trading posts.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Added 3 Raider characteres known from Endzone - A World Apart, each with own bunkers and vehicles.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Raiders now attack settlements with artillery. A tribute can be payed to stop the attack or to lower the intensity.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Raiders now steal your resources if they successfully attacked a settlement.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Raider vehicles now roam the map in mid- to late-game, turning the wasteland into dangerous, shifting territory.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Raider bunkers spawn across the map, creating new threats that challenge your movement and decision-making in the badlands.
[b]Raiders:[/b] New achievements reward those who take the fight to the raiders.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Added new VFX, including smoke, debris, and muffled impact effects that amplify the chaos.
[b]Raiders:[/b] A new sub-tutorial helps you survive the raider threat... or at least understand what killed you.
[b]Raiders:[/b] Added a new game goal that focusses on defeating raiders. 
[/p][table noborder="1" equalcells="1" colwidth="340,"][tr][td colwidth="340"][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2372dae5a3ada01dd49d667b8464118ff448223b.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/9de22311e76c2846dbcddd3df7fef9902c528bdb.png"][/img][/p][/td][td][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/47badb521f6d279c0185ff738c3f420ff3d380ed.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/b6563f3b20f437ed70387dbb1b7091704ef2d407.png"][/img][/p][/td][/tr][/table][p][b]UI:[/b] Info for seed rating replaced with stars and new tooltip.
[b]UI:[/b] Implemented notification for zone attack events.
[b]UI:[/b] Added notification for destroyed interzone buildings.
[b]UI:[/b] Added minimap ping for constructed vehicles.
[b]UI:[/b] Added repair info to unit health bars.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] Destroyed vehicles now leave a wreck that can be looted.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] Most vehicles can now be equipped with weapon items in order to attack or defend.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] The behaviour of vehicles can now be set to aggressive or defensive.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/38c7b7e09d6369437e312fc029f0bd5e11468a28.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Buildings:[/b] Fixed sandmine crashes and power pole visibility.
[b]Buildings:[/b] Decontaminators now profit from electricity.
[b]Events:[/b] Tutorial zone reveal for invalid zones now triggers correctly.
[b]Events:[/b] Fixed dialog for some events of the same type being not correctly displayed.
[b]Expeditions:[/b] Fixed various gameplay and localization issues.
[b]Gameplay:[/b] Fixed multiple minimap display issues and UI highlights.
[b]Gameplay:[/b] Fixed lags when sending vehicles by improving pathfinding logic.
[b]Localization:[/b] Fixed various localization issues.
[b]Repair:[/b] Several stability and bug fixes for damaged buildings after sandstorms.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/281a82ab4ce953a75b80e435c91f0f8f2de2dc31.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]Expeditions:[/b] Camera now moves to new explorer position when explorer is teleported (e.g. in vents).
[b]UI:[/b] Removed branch dropdown and feedback buttons from main menu.
[b]UI:[/b] Improved HUD layout and LargeMap elements.
[b]UI:[/b] The resource list in the HUD can now be expanded to have an overview of all resources.
[b]UI:[/b] Notification sounds now have a delay to prevent sound spamming.
[b]Radiation:[/b] Decontaminatiors now require decontamination kits to remove ground radiation.
[b]Radiation:[/b] Removed Decontamination Kits from settler radiation protection.
[b]Seeds:[/b] Caoutchouc is no unlocked from the beginning.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] Vehicle physics adjusted to prevent overlapping.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] Wheels of vehicles no longer move away from the chassis when moving on slopes.
[b]Vehicles:[/b] Selectable vehicles now show group index for better identification.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png"][/img] [/p][h2]🔧 Get into 1.0 – And Let Us Know What You Think![/h2][p]We’re incredibly excited about the full release update and can’t wait to hear your feedback about the newly added Raiders. notes.notes:
Survivors,

This update delivers [b]different quality-of-life improvements[/b] and [b]long-requested UI upgrades[/b] to make your time in Endzone 2 smoother than ever. One highlight is the [b]"transfer all" button for looting ruins[/b] that has finally made it into the game.

We’ve also made a [b]key change to controls[/b]: the [b]number keys (1–0)[/b] are now dedicated to assigning and selecting vehicle groups, giving you [b]quicker access to your fleet[/b]. [b]Game speed controls[/b] have been moved to [b]new shortcuts[/b] to accommodate this change.

As always, we’ve tackled a range of bugs and stability issues across the board—from UI glitches to rare savegame problems—ensuring a more polished and reliable experience.

Thanks for all your feedback—keep it coming!

notes.title: #8 | Major Update | Dangers & Progression ☢️⚠️NOW LIVE
notes.notes:
[b]Survivors,[/b]

We’ve just deployed our [b]biggest update[/b] yet for [b]Endzone 2[/b], and it’s going to challenge everything you know about [b]survival in the wasteland[/b]. From [b]radiation rework[/b] and brand-new buildings, to [b]deadly weather[/b] and [b]disease mechanics[/b] – the [b]Dangers & Progression[/b] update is live now!

This update also squashes bugs like [b]building placement issues[/b] and [b]expedition glitches[/b] for smoother play. Some tweaks make things even better, with stronger sandstorms, a refreshed disease system, and clearer radiation visuals. Updated tutorials make jumping in a breeze, pulling you deeper into this post-apocalyptic adventure!

[previewyoutube=oCRKG3McEGA;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Update Highlights Breakdown[/h2]

[h3][b]Major radiation system overhaul[/b][/h3]
→ Includes a detailed radiation overlay, cleansing rain, and irradiated food & water mechanics

[h3][b]New buildings[/b][/h3]
→ Decontaminator, Brewery, Bar, Coffee Shop, and more

[h3][b] New resources[/b][/h3]
→ Hops and Weed, used in beer and joint production

[h3][b]Upgraded storage buildings[/b][/h3]
→ Now remove radiation from food and water

[h3][b]4 new expeditions[/b][/h3]
→ Sewage Plant, Hospital, Traffic Accident, Small Ominous House

[h3][b] Game goal overhaul[/b][/h3]
→ New goal selection menu and 3 themed win conditions

[h3][b]Late-game content[/b][/h3]
→ Unlock Beacon monument and decorative statues through new missions

[h3][b]New missions & improved tutorials[/b][/h3]
→ Guides for new mechanics and content

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h2]☢️A New Era of Radiation☢️[/h2]
Radiation has evolved into a full survival mechanic. You’ll now need to:

[list]
[*] Monitor zone-based radiation with a new overlay
[*] Watch out for irradiated food and water
[*] Build Decontaminators and upgraded storage buildings to fight back
[*] Hope for cleansing rain – it now removes radiation naturally
[*] This rework adds new complexity, new visuals, and new threats.
[/list]

notes.notes:
Hey Survivors!

Surviving the dangers of the wasteland is one thing. But what comes after survival? What keeps you going when your people are thriving, your cities are growing, and the sandstorms finally pass?

In today’s sneak peek, we’ll take a closer look at the "Progression" half of our upcoming [b]Dangers & Progression[/b] update — giving you new ways to shape your journey, define your victories, and push your settlements to the next level.

Let’s take a look...

[*] [b]Long-Term Survival[/b] – Endure 200 seasons
[*] [b]Expansionist[/b] – Create a total of 9 settlements[/list]
Completing a goal [b]earns you a shiny new achievement[/b] and the opportunity to [b]conclude[/b] the session. But don’t worry — you can always keep playing if your story isn’t finished yet.

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Dangers & Progression Pt.1☢️⚠️
notes.notes:
Hey survivors!

Hope your settlements are holding strong—because in our next major update, [b]Dangers & Progression[/b], we’re dialing things up a notch! While there’s plenty to talk about (yes, custom victory goals are coming!), today we want to give you a [b]first glimpse[/b] at something that’s been simmering beneath the surface: [b]the overhaul of environmental dangers[/b].

Let’s take a look at what’s coming soon...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a77b4f432ae561ef245fbbef207adacca70ea038.png[/img]

From [b]reworked radiation zones[/b] to [b]deadlier sandstorms[/b] and [b]disease outbreaks[/b] that’ll really put your survival strategies to the test, the wasteland is becoming even [b]more unforgiving[/b]—and we couldn’t be more excited.

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Radiation Rework – A Deeper Threat Beneath Your Feet[/b][/u][/h3]

[b]Radiation [/b]is no longer just a simple value tied to each zone. Instead, it now [b]directly affects[/b] the ground itself. [b]Contaminated rain[/b] will irradiate the soil, while [b]clean rain[/b] helps decontaminate it over time.

A [b]brand-new overlay[/b] lets you view [b]ground radiation levels[/b], adding a strategic layer to building placement. [b]Constructing buildings on contaminated ground[/b] will raise your settlement’s overall radiation level—exposing your settlers to danger unless they’re equipped with [b]protective clothing[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/d4e7f9b991d2eb9821876cdbf3be9d47130c7c22.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/b104b8deed51493dd57f0dad0491e8e29e98f9c9.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Resources gathered from irradiated ground—like [b]food [/b]and [b]water[/b]—can now [b]contaminate [/b]a zone’s storage, [b]spreading the risk [/b]even further.

This system brings back some [b]familiar mechanics from Endzone 1[/b], requiring players to [b]think carefully[/b] about where they build and how they manage radiation to [b]keep their people safe[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5ffcbea62cf3d47d285042e2844cd2ef9b828eb7.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5ca16810c9f9ebc51146e6bc72a4f666eca59966.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Sandstorm Rework – No Longer Just Dust in the Wind[/b][/u][/h3]

The old "[i]Sanded[/i]" zone state is gone for good. Sandstorms now [b]pack a real punch[/b]—each time one strikes, some of your [b]buildings will take damage[/b].

If a building becomes [b]fully damaged[/b], it’ll [b]stop functioning[/b] until it’s repaired. Just like construction, repairs are handled by your [b]unemployed settlers[/b] and will require [b]resources to complete[/b].

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/33a95c022586c389e37eda181f60adc55d9decb6.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/84975ec9a03afd7ec77f74009bb4c41298c7ba33.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
To help you stay in control, you can now [b]disable all repairs[/b] in any given zone if needed—perfect for when [b]resources are tight[/b] or [b]priorities shift[/b].

This [b]new system[/b] turns sandstorms into a dynamic, ongoing threat that [b]forces tough decisions[/b] about what to fix, when, and where.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/82d210ba3c8980ec5fbf45fd792821b248601123.png[/img][/th]
        [th]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2675af4c72a0208cd0b7298f7bb36cbd60ad26f7.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Diseases[/b][/u][/h3]

The old "[i]Sick[/i]" zone state has been [b]removed[/b]. Now, when a [b]disease outbreak[/b] occurs, it [b]directly affects[/b] your settlers—several are randomly selected and become sick.

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7d329e7a0f1669b1fbe827a2a04b4d420d41769c.png[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/415e1ba167478f38473baf7bc0db808a8e8bcbc4.png[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
Sick settlers are [b]unable to work[/b] and will stay that way [b]until they recover[/b]. Recovery can happen [b]naturally over time[/b] or be sped up by [b]visiting a hospital[/b]—just one of the new buildings from the upcoming update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/551186c21d25ead3fd5f8ae08a3cd45ec9626c27.png[/img]
This rework puts the [b]focus on individual well-being[/b] rather than a broad zone effect, making disease a [b]more personal[/b] and [b]impactful challenge[/b] to manage.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

That’s all for now—but it’s only the beginning. We’ll be sharing more details soon about the second major part of this update: [b]Progression[/b]. You’ll be able to [b]define your own goals[/b] for each play session, giving you even [b]more control[/b] over how you survive and thrive in the wasteland. 

And that’s not all! Also part of the Progression topic, the update will bring [b]new buildings[/b], [b]fresh expeditions[/b], and [b]plenty of other additions[/b] to explore.

As always, a [b]huge thank you[/b] for your continued [b]support[/b], [b]feedback[/b], and [b]encouragement [/b]across Steam, Discord, and beyond. You’re helping shape the future of [b]Endzone 2[/b], and we can’t wait to show you what’s next. 💚

notes.notes:
Survivors,

A new wave of improvements has arrived! This update introduces [b]Education[/b], featuring [b]Schools[/b], [b]Paper Mills[/b], and a system where settlers [b]earn Badges[/b] that [b]grant buffs[/b] to [b]settlement buildings[/b] and [b]expeditions[/b]. Children now grow into the next generation, and the [b]Bulletin Board[/b] helps settlers [b]notify you of new missions[/b]. Expeditions expand with the [b]new Endzone and Airfield sites[/b], while [b]Modding [/b]gets a [b]soft launch[/b] for early experimentation.

We've also added [b]Upcycling improvements[/b], including [b]new ruins[/b] like the [b]Park[/b], [b]Hospital[/b], and[b] Fish Farm[/b], plus [b]"Find Trader"[/b] missions. Settlers now have [b]improved life cycles and visuals[/b], making your world feel more alive.

Finally, [b]numerous fixes[/b] and [b]tweaks enhance the UI[/b], [b]pathfinding[/b], [b]missions[/b], and [b]expeditions[/b], alongside [b]balancing updates[/b] for [b]radiation[/b], [b]trade[/b], and [b]resources[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

Last but not least this update also includes our [b]first iteration of Modding support[/b]!

Modding was a [b]highly requested feature[/b], and it was on our list from the [b]very beginning of Endzone 2’s development[/b]. Now, we’re thrilled to introduce the [b]very first moddable version[/b] of the game! [b]It’s still in its early stages[/b], but already allows you to [b]mod several textures, sprites, audio files, and even add your own localizations[/b].

[/table]
We chose [b]mod.io[/b] as our platform to handle mods, as it gives us the ability to also enable [b]modding for the whole player base across multiple platforms[/b].

[b]Disclaimer:[/b] [i]Please be aware that modding capabilities are still very limited but we want to put this out early to get early feedback and harden the infrastructure. [/i]

To help you get started, we’ve put together a [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3430275798]comprehensive Modding Guide[/url]. Happy modding!

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Education & Bulletin Board 🎒📋
notes.notes:
Survivors!

The release of our next major update, [b]Education & Bulletin Board[/b], is fast approaching! To get you excited, we’re offering a [b]sneak peek[/b] at what’s coming your way. So, without further ado—let’s dive in!

Just like in our previous sneak peek, here’s some [b]basic information[/b] about the [b]main features[/b] of this update:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/4d1728b77b18bddf689de56915fdd581a34b552a.png[/img]

With this update and the newly introduced overall theme [b]Education[/b], you can shape your settlements' future early on. Because [b]Education is key[/b]!

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Schools[/b][/u][/h3]

Schools are the heart of learning, [b]employing dedicated teachers[/b] who help pave the path forward. As long as a teacher is present, children can attend—and when they [b]grow up[/b], they receive a [b]Badge[/b], marking their journey into the next stage of life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/919ca02d185aabcee9539709e41fc2e494b631c9.png[/img]
The type of [b]Badge [/b]a child earns is influenced by [b]you, the player[/b]. Each Zone offers a[b] variety of available Badges[/b], and you decide which ones are allowed. When a child grows up, they have an equal chance of receiving any permitted Badge. For example, if three Badges are available, each has a [b]⅓ probability of being awarded[/b]. However, a child can only ever receive one Badge—making your choices even more impactful.

There are [b]several Badges[/b], each providing [b]unique bonuses and drawbacks[/b] that influence different aspects of the game. Every Settler with a Badge [b]contributes a portion of its effect[/b] to the entire zone, subtly [b]shaping its dynamics[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1a94b20b2a180a8a16d332100fb4d0349c95638e.png[/img]
Every school has a [b]set number[/b] of student slots. If more children are present in a Zone than the school can accommodate, [b]not all of them[/b] will receive a Badge when they grow up. Managing space wisely ensures [b]the best possible future[/b] for your young citizens!

A thriving school also needs resources. Therefore, [b]schools consume paper[/b] while operating, so keeping your supply stocked [b]ensures smooth learning[/b].

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Papermill[/b][/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/27905cdd491e956be61c0777d87b552c71f6f70e.png[/img]
[b]Paper[/b]—how do we get it? Glad you asked! Paper can be produced in the [b]Papermill[/b], a [b]new building[/b] introduced in this update. The [b]Papermill [/b]creates paper using water and reed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/c451fc5d8993df8bd7ea3b8b46d7520b984137fb.png[/img]
Introducing [b]Reed[/b]—a versatile new crop for your [b]Swamp Farm[/b]! Hardy and resilient, this resource [b]thrives in wetland conditions[/b], offering [b]new opportunities for crafting and production[/b]. Keep your farms flourishing and make the most of this [b]valuable addition[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/8dbd01652536a20861e93afe53a9c8791b84278e.png[/img]

The introduction of [b]Bulletin Boards[/b] gives your settlers a voice—and you the opportunity to listen. At the Bulletin Board, you'll receive settlers' requests that can boost their contentment, as well as quests that help improve your settlement. Completing these tasks may reward you with additional resources and other valuable benefits. The Bulletin Board can be [b]found[/b] at your [b]Town Center[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ca3e5f4682e1555f76a514ed8e60ea3cdd94c817.png[/img]
A variety of [b]events and quests[/b] are tied to the Bulletin Board, unfolding throughout your session. Be sure to [b]check the board regularly[/b], or your settlers' overall [b]contentedness may decline[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/8a4890ddc5efed909de8e584c7280d709cb9debc.png[/img]
[b]On a side note[/b]: You’ll now receive [b]fewer direct event dialogues[/b], as many of these events will be [b]redirected to the Bulletin Board[/b] for you to review at your convenience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

Besides these two big topics, [b]the update[/b] will bring [b]a lot more to the game[/b] which we will cover in the update's [b]comprehensive changelog next week[/b]. 🔥

Until then, feel free to share your [b]thoughts[/b], [b]feedback[/b], and [b]ideas[/b]—particularly about the [b]features mentioned[/b] in this posting. 

Thank you for your ongoing support. Talk soon!

This update brings exciting [b]new additions[/b] and [b]improvements[/b] to enhance your journey! [b]Traders[/b] now populate the world, offering unique loot, reputation missions, and an engaging bargaining system. The intermediate area [b]connects zones with electricity[/b] using new power poles, a construction vehicle, and a detailed electricity overview. [h3][u][b]Spotlight: Rusty's Shop[/b][/u][/h3]

Each trader has their own [b]unique Trading Post[/b] located somewhere in the badlands. The screenshot below showcases [b]Rusty's shop[/b], where you'll meet the feisty and good-humored trader [b]Rusty Rolph[/b], always ready with a snappy saying to brighten your day.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/3ce971b46cc7ab95f2afc378e82580ac7424f14c.png[/img]
Bargaining with a trader can be tricky, so make sure to keep them satisfied with your offers. Otherwise, they might lose patience, and you'll [b]risk damaging your reputation[/b] with them.

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Hunting Lodge[/b][/u][/h3]

As mentioned in the introduction, the [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] is a new building in [b]Endzone 2[/b] that supplies your settlement with food. What makes the [b]Hunting Lodge[/b] unique is that its production [b]remains consistent even during a drought[/b]—setting it apart from other food sources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/86fac5fcaf01abed0fe6f143ad75aa9dfafdb852.png[/img]
[b]Wildlife will now spawn in zones[/b] to support food production. For now, there are two types of animals: [b]deer [/b]and [b]boars[/b]. However, be cautious not to overhunt them—they need time to recover and repopulate.

notes.title: [Sneak Peek] Major Update | Electricity & Upcycling 💡
notes.notes:
Survivors!

The Major update, called [b]Electricity & Upcycling[/b], is just around the corner. We'd like to give you a sneak peek at the content of this update, so let's get started.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/841d2081384fd7478522abec59f226f3f3d3a724.png[/img]

Before jumping into details, here's what Electricity does in Endzone 2 in a nutshell: It allows you to generate and distribute power in your zones. This will be possible with new buildings that will be added in this update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Relay Station[/b][/u][/h3]

The Relay Station is the key building for electricity distribution within your settlements—there won’t be any light without it. Only producers and consumers connected to the Relay Station via electricity poles can feed in or consume energy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/1efd32a8ba4a0203a606c9225dbbfbd7168f54f2.png[/img]
The Relay Station also provides detailed information about the amount of electricity stored and the number of connected buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Wind Turbine[/b][/u][/h3]

The Wind Turbine is the most basic building for electricity production in Endzone 2. To put it bluntly, it converts wind into electricity and feeds it into the Relay Station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/4fab6a112eba33e9d265b8a965e202a1fa7ff4a8.png[/img]
There are actually two versions of the Wind Turbine: one is a standard electricity building available after being researched, and the other is part of the new upcycling feature. So, let’s jump right into it.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/b64bffdb48ac8ab3608d465e4fb98620f010ff5c.png[/img]

Upcycling has been a highly coveted feature since the early stages of Endzone, and now we’re super excited to finally make it happen. We can now implement the ability to re-use specific ruins available on the map. You’ve just learned about the Wind Turbine ruin, so here’s another one for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Upcycled Wind Turbine[/b][/u][/h3]

Remember those big, weathered Wind Turbines? Well, now they can be re-used to produce electricity—after being overhauled using the necessary resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/03ba7da0e3859a5eef870e75a7097e338977119c.png[/img]

This is just one of the ruins that can be upcycled, and it’s literally a kick-start for your settlement’s bright future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[h3][u][b]Spotlight: Old/Restored warehouse[/b][/u][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/a67e90548df60d02a562aa533aca91329f76a51e.png[/img]
These old warehouses can be restored by paying the construction costs. Once restored, they can make a big difference for your settlement, as they are designed to store a large quantity of resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5635299938ebb7b55b3f7936e379f0c891dc033f.png[/img]
Both of these newly introduced features are just the beginning, laying the foundation for even more exciting features we'd like to add to the world of Endzone 2. Electricity is another anchor that allows us to implement more advanced technologies with future updates. The same goes for Upcycling, where the possibilities for additional ruins and enhanced immersion are vast.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

We’re eagerly looking forward to your thoughts, feedback, and ideas—especially regarding these two features. 

That's actually a great transition over to our very first question of the week: What kinds of re-usable ruins would you like to see in future updates? Let us know on [url=https://discord.com/invite/worldofendzone]Discord[/url] or in the comments.

Thank you for your ongoing support. Talk to you soon!

notes.title: Endzone 2 | Early Access Release | OUT NOW
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/682168a8ed516b6c6030e61dcb4f700806e0579f.gif[/img]

Alright, survivors. Here we are again, launching into Early Access with Endzone and starting a journey that is already, and will continue to be, heavily impacted by your feedback. Developing Endzone 2 is a balancing act between trying out new things and staying true to the original IP. Throughout Early Access, we expect to close this gap together with you and find that perfect sweet spot for the post-apocalyptic city-builder we all wish for.

[h3]Let's bring it on![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/41a86b24b00f5d130cb9bfca44d5b2340bce4ac7.png[/img]
[previewyoutube=MgBnD8CJUoQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/f076163ad40c35e27d47490bace1f2fcd12238f6.png[/img]
[list]
[*] Endzone 2 is not a cozy or completely relaxed city builder. You can customize it extensively and almost turn it into one, but at its core, it's about ensuring the survival of your settlements.
[*] It's not a fast-paced RTS game where every unit is interactable or movable, like in Age of Empires or Starcraft. While we have introduced vehicles and interactive expeditions, where you directly control your units, creating and managing settlements is done on a per-building basis.
[*] While you may notice several similarities to the Anno series, Endzone 2 is more focused on exploring new locations directly on the map. Ruins can be scavenged, and you can experience expeditions firsthand by moving your explorers. You don't leave the map—everything happens directly in the game world.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/8544709d7ded7206c4389100958db42f17c31b19.png[/img]
The Roadmap always highlights the next two upcoming game updates based on our internal plans. So, here are the first two for you to check out:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/0879ce06c745263d6db00a5da21431be7fe999a2.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]
[b]The first patch currently includes[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixes for reported bugs
[*] Stability improvements
[*] Quality of Life improvements
[/list]
[b]The first content update is called Let There Be Light! and includes[/b]
[list]
[*] Electricity: Generate and distribute electricity!
[*] Upcycling: Turn specific ruins into buildings!
[*] Content: New side missions and POIs
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/7f8196eb03fa8b49229b48a4712bc4cfceee085b.png[/img]
[b]Please note:[/b] During the Early Access phase of Endzone - A World Apart, we pushed out big feature updates monthly. [b]With Endzone 2, we now split the update stream into a monthly rotation of patches and major updates.[/b] This will allow us to integrate more feature-rich and coherent additions with the major updates, as it gives us more time to invest in QA and feature iteration.

[b]Patches[/b] will include quality of life improvements, balancing changes, and bug fixes. They might also feature smaller content additions or changes.

[b]Major Updates[/b] will introduce significant features, such as Electricity (see Roadmap). A major update might also include substantial content additions, like a thematic set of new missions or expeditions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/844eb56eb887d0af1c529b74ed4292af6034e324.png[/img]
Just like with Endzone - A World Apart, we want to develop Endzone 2 together with you, its community. Releasing Endzone 2 into Early Access is one of the biggest milestones we've achieved since we began working on the game.

We want to emphasize that the community is extremely important to us and is practically essential for the development of Endzone 2. With your help and dedication, we aim to gain clear insights into which features are desired and how we can further improve the game for players. We've seen many times how games that started off great failed to adapt to the voice of their player base. Our goal is to remain transparent throughout development, stay open-minded, and listen to our community.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/ba1a6f1530490cc3c927b0844bb6a19fb21dba26.png[/img]
We want to hear your thoughts! Do not hesitate, so please go forth and report any bug or feedback via in-game reporting Tool. [b]Press F2[/b] and describe how the bug occurred or pick the Feedback tag and tell us how we can improve Endzone 2. Please don't write support inquiries via email, use our in-game reporting tool. 

As for your feedback, we have created an easy way for you to leave or post feedback directly from within the game. Additionally, you can also reach out to us on [url=https://discord.com/invite/worldofendzone]Discord[/url], Steam or with our dedicated feedback form! 

You can also provide feedback without using the in-game tool: 

[b]Feedback:[/b] https://form.asana.com/?k=KyMLfw3gfCkIEyVPz3m3KA&d=1192678870065366   
[b]Bugs:[/b] https://form.asana.com/?k=uPWxYt_u8JsfagkF1rUUfw&d=1192678870065366 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/e2792aa5c814b05c115d2a1d075c6d71004a38e0.png[/img]
Since this is an Early Access release, please note that the game may enter a state where it isn't entirely stable, meaning there are a few known issues. We've created a short list of these issues to inform you that we're working on fixing them as soon as possible.

[b]Please note:[/b] If an error occurs in the background, it will be transparently displayed with a popup on your screen. If that happens, we would greatly appreciate it if you could send us a bug report using our in-game bug reporter. If the pop-up happens, we recommend not to continue with your current game sessions. It is recommended to restart the game due to consecutive errors as a result of the initial error.
[list]
[*] [b]Low Bitrate while streaming:[/b] Please turn off “sharpen” in the options menu. You find it in Options>Graphics>Render Quality.
[*] [b]Building Upgrades:[/b] Players may experience issues when they upgrade buildings.
[*] [b]Pink screen/game crashing on startup/VULKAN dialog:[/b] We’ve released an update to fix this issue. If it still occurs, please refer to our guide for further troubleshooting.
[*] [b]Localization:[/b] Please be aware that some localization strings may be missing or displayed incorrectly.
[*] [b]Voice Over:[/b] Some POIs (Expeditions) and Event based lines are still missing their voice overs; these will be implemented soon.
[*] [b]Black screen after the loading screen:[/b] When starting a new game round, certain session settings may cause the game to briefly display a black screen immediately after the loading screen before the game round begins.
[*] [b]Map Creator:[/b] Disabling large and medium-sized zones can lead to unusable/erroneous maps.
[/list][h3]Thank you for your understanding.[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/84617fd982335c9a3805707079ed684861843337.png[/img]
Okay, let's not turn this into a novel. We hope you enjoy playing Endzone 2 and that the wait was worthwhile. We're very much looking forward to your feedback and can't wait to go on this journey together with you.

THANK YOU!
The teams @ Gentlymad Studios & Assemble Entertainment

notes.title: Developer Blog Post - Changes & Reworks based on YOUR Feedback
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/5c3f28c297c4786a52261c5f716556682419a825.gif[/img]

[b]Survivors,

The demo for Endzone 2 has been out for a while now, and the amount of feedback we’ve received has been incredible. Many of you pointed out various aspects of the game that did not live up to your expectations and needed improvement. Some changes however we made transitioning from Endzone - A World Apart were welcomed and received positive feedback, which is why we conducted a [b]survey[/b] a few weeks ago, based on that very feedback.

We have evaluated the results, discussed them in our team, and made many changes based on your input. Before we dive into how Endzone 2 has developed since the demo version, we want to thank you for your massive support, interest, and care for the game. We carefully read every report and incorporate your feedback as much as possible.[/b]

[b]So, let’s jump into what we’ve addressed so far:[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Settlers & Immersion:[/h3][/u]
One of the most frequent feedback points was the lack of simulation in Endzone 2, making the game feel lifeless as settlers were not well integrated into the world. [b]We enhanced this by adding new animations, such as carrying tools, moving cartwheels, working in and on buildings, and even loafing around and sitting on benches.[/b] The [b]“Wuselfaktor”[/b] has been increased, making the settlement buzz with life.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/4eb1c3e32df6cc599d94eb630a25f812c86ab080.png[/img]
[i]Carry visuals for the settlers[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/f830211bb4470b1b40dfc88f0469cb452ec2560a.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/3b9ec590f76053383e92f3efc6697bb56f5bdd01.gif[/img]

Settlers are now clickable again, showing their unique portrait and current activities. Additionally they reflect the state of the settlement regarding health, confidence and radiation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/d0c4b7242fc03f0276359abe9a7b09fc84740864.gif[/img]

We are continuously improving the settlers' interactions and adding more features. Our goal is to create an organic, living settlement that you can follow and get immersed in.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Research System:[/h3][/u]
The interface and mechanics of the [b]Research System[/b] have been redesigned. Reports indicated that many of you did not like how it was set up. Some users had issues understanding what could be researched, while others were unhappy with how easy and instant research could be conducted. We saw the issues and made changes. Progressing in the Tech Tree still requires Knowledge Points, which can only be obtained by [b]progressing in expeditions[/b]. Now, every expedition can yield a new Knowledge Point, making it unnecessary to search for specific expeditions. Once a point is obtained, new buildings can be unlocked for research in the research window. [b]Technologies then can be researched by spending certain resources[/b]. After choosing a new technology, a timer shows the progress of the research.
[b]You can also skip layers in the research tree, allowing you to research at your own pace depending on your needs.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/22d1bec97f8fb64bd28eee55206d0e870c169f7e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Settlement Branches & Housing[/h3][/u]
Settlement Branches now only categorize buildings by their respective areas in the Tech Tree. [b]We removed the different Housing Types and the boost in productivity from houses placed close to production buildings.[/b] This system frustrated most of you and made no sense, as placing buildings close to a production chain and far away would be both beneficial and bad at the same time. This is why we simply removed it for now.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Confidence System:[/h3][/u]
The confidence system has been reworked, tying the confidence of your settlement to each individual house. Your settlement starts with a base value of [b]50 out of 100 confidence[/b], which can be influenced positively or negatively by certain conditions. [b]Community buildings[/b] near housing districts improve settlers' mood, while living close to production facilities lowers it due to noise and pollution. All houses contribute to a [b]global confidence value[/b] for your zone. High confidence can trigger positive events, such as [b]festivals or new settlers joining[/b], while low confidence can lead to negative events, such as [b]people leaving or stealing supplies.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/806a0854743cd68016fcffc3caf80cb0f870d230.png[/img]

Tier 1 buildings of your early settlement can only reach a value up to 70. Upgraded houses and advancing technology and prosperity will allow for higher values. Maintaining a constant supply of food, water, and medicine is also crucial. A lack of these resources, high radiation levels, and unattended corpses will negatively impact confidence.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Health System:[/h3][/u]
The health system works similarly to the confidence system and can be affected by the same factors. If people are supplied with medicine and not exposed to radiation, [b]overall resistance to diseases is high[/b]. The lower your health value drops, the higher the chance of a disease outbreak. [b]The severity and duration[/b] of a disease depends on the overall health condition of your settlers at outbreak.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Wells:[/h3][/u]
The survey showed that many players were unhappy with the requirement of placing a well in a swamp. Therefore we decided that [b]wells can be placed anywhere[/b]. On top we also added a [b]"Water Purifying Facility"[/b] that instead can only be placed in swamp areas, which works more effectively than a regular well and also fits the realism aspect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2d337b1cee8038da6562b341860ef11c43475dbb.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Zone Establishment:[/h3][/u]
Feedback indicated that starting a new settlement was too complex and poorly communicated. Many players struggled to even get started, so we reworked the system. Now, when approaching a new zone, the Landing Stage, essential for Transport Routes and logistics, [b]will automatically snap to a viable position[/b]. The Blueprint will dynamically change based on your vehicle's position, allowing for easy placement with a simple click. The camera then moves to the center of the zone with the [b]Town Center already selected[/b]. This process is more readable and faster.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/0ef2aa6de8807958988dc4ed193a517bfd0f6fbc.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Expeditions:[/h3][/u]
The survey showed that most of you wanted [b]more variety and complexity in expeditions[/b]. We introduced a new [b]Item System[/b] that interconnects expeditions through key items needed for progression. Some places may require a lock-pick, a ladder, or a generator to progress. These items can now be carried separately from resources and taken to another expedition where they are needed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/eda046530394b9e84e34d63dd57e2db3f0afe3c9.png[/img]

This increases the need for and reward from exploring each expedition carefully. We also created more unique expedition locations to reduce repetitiveness. You can now visit locations like the famous [b]Nuclear Power Plant from Endzone - A World Apart[/b], the largest expedition we’ve designed so far.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/2e18df4528a105a13501a0c963b9adb2f9633780.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Decorations:[/h3][/u]
Many of you asked for decoration options to enhance your settlement's visuals. With Early Access, we are introducing an initial batch of decoration buildings, which we will continue to add to. Here is a collection of the buildings you will be able to place:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/e63d7dd193da7497765a5d9bbd6d5f70ec68d7cc.png[/img]

These include:
[list]
[*]Birch
[*]Larch
[*]Flag
[*]Statue
[*]Garden
[*]Small Flowerbed
[*]Medium Flowerbed
[*]Large Flowerbed
[*]Bench
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Community Buiildings:[/h3][/u]
In conjunction with the new decorations, there is also a new type of buildings, that has decorative elements to it, but directly impact the confidence systems. [b]Community Buildings are a place for your settlers to hang out, meet and relax.[/b]

Those include:
[list]
[b][*]Campfire[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/eedbd53f8c9e45616460344707adf19028406d9a.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/96f3878bc5b1ab62e1ad85e84530a3e8c0cd1c5c.gif[/img]

[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44535526/54a023f03a740c71dee4e51699201190f49488ef.png[/img]

[u][h3]Readability of Buildings:[/h3][/u]
Many reports indicated that some buildings looked too similar or were not distinguishable from afar. [b]We reworked all buildings mentioned in this feedback[/b], also tweaking their colors and shapes to make them unique and recognizable from any camera distance. In addition, a few new buildings have been introduced. With these changes we came closer to how we want buildings to look in general, fitting the post-apocalyptic setting they are placed in.

[u][h3]General Quality Of Life Improvements:[/h3][/u]
[list]
[*] Blueprint-Mode that can be toggled and automatically activates, if the needed resources are not available.
[*] Dynamic Cloud Shadow to increase immersion.
[*] Improved foliage distribution for a more organic environment.
[*] Added Vignette for the camera
[*] Resources can be deleted from inventory
[/list]

[u][h3]Conclusion:[/h3][/u]
Although all systems have been touched and partially reworked, everything is still a work in progress. A few examples of what we are currently working on include children, builders at construction sites, and the general interactions of settlers as we can still improve on the overall “Fluff”.
Throughout Early Access, we will keep our eyes and ears open to your feedback, constantly adjusting systems and mechanics as we did with the demo.

notes.title: Updated Release Schedule
notes.notes:
Fellow Survivors,

We hope this message finds you well! Today we have an important update to share with you regarding the journey of Endzone 2, a project you're supporting with incredible enthusiasm - and we are still extremely thankful for that!

After much consideration and internal discussions, the teams at Gentlymad and Assemble Entertainment have together decided to move the release of the Early Access version of Endzone 2 from Spring 2024 to Summer 2024.

We are totally aware of and understand that this will disappoint some of you, but we assure you: This decision was not made lightly - and the reason for this decision was made with a singular goal in mind: to deliver the extraordinary gaming experience you, our players, both expect and deserve!

The additional development time will be used to ensure that Endzone 2 meets the high quality standards we set for ourselves right from the start of the Early Access phase. Our commitment to excellence and to your satisfaction remains our number one priority, so we hope you understand this decision. 

To give you a glimpse of the development progress, we're excited to share some new screenshots showcasing the development journey so far. These images reflect the hard work and dedication of the whole development team and hint at the exciting world the awesome people working at Gentlymad are crafting for you.
